# dsh-sidebar-restart

One row in the sidebar foot, beside the settings gear: restarts the DSH desktop
app in a single clic
k, instead of quitting from the tray and relaunching by hand.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or straight from the repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart the app once by hand so the plugin loads — which is the last time you
have to do that,
since this button is what you use from then on.

**Desktop only.** On a plain `dsh web` profile the row renders disabled and says
why; there is no de

sktop process to replace there. If you wanted the *Web server*
restarted, that is a different plugin
(`dsh-restart-button`).
## What it does, in one line

Adds a **Restart** row to the desktop app's sidebar foot beside Settings. Clicking
it asks the Host

to restart; a detached helper kills the Electron main process and
the Host by PID, waits until both

are gone, starts the app again, and the tab
reloads itself once the replacement answers with a new b

oot id — so a plugin you
installed a moment ago is actually running afterwards.
## What it looks like
| Desktop app (wide sidebar) | Mobile drawer |

Both follow the host's own rule rather than a breakpoint of mine: the label appears
exactly where th

e host shows one for the gear, i.e. when the sidebar is wide. In the
narrow 56px rail the row stays
icon-only and keeps the gear's 36×36 target.
## The control is a copy of the gear row next door

The seat is `sidebar.footer.action` — "optional actions beside Settings at the
sidebar foot". The sh

ipped sidebar renders it as `footerActions`, a flex row that
`footArea` lays out **above** `settings

Area` (the gear row). So in the plain host
footer this control sits directly above the gear.

It is deliberately styled as the gear's twin, with every value read from the
shipped `.wCInkW_trigge

r` (ui-settings-general) and the seat's own sibling
`.dsh-mobile-control__trigger`, which agree:
| Property | Value | Why |
| colour | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` | the gear uses the **primary** label colour; a secondary-col

oured icon beside it is a visible mismatch |
| height | `42px` | the footer row height both host con

trols use |
| padding | `0 10px 0 8px`, `gap 8px` | the gear's own padding and icon/label gap |
| ra

dius | `--dsw-radius-md` | the gear's radius, not the small one |
| label | `14px / 22px`, `font: in

herit` | the gear label's typography |
| row box | `calc(100% + 4px)`, `margin 4px -2px` | the gear'
s row is `.wCInkW_triggerRow{width:calc(100% + 4px);margin:4px -2px}` — it bleeds 2px past the colum
n on each side, so its content begins at `parentLeft − 2 + 8 = +6`. Without the same bleed this row'
s icon **and** label sit 2px to the right of the gear's, and the two never line up. This button *is*
its own row, so it carries both the bleed and the padding. |

Verified on a **real phone screenshot** (1216×2640, so ≈3.5 device px per CSS px),
measuring the dar
k ink of each row directly:
| row, on the device | icon ink left | label ink left | icon ink | row centre |

| before the bleed: 重启 | `73` | `157` | 50 | `2356.5` |
| before the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 |

`2531.5` |
| after the bleed: 重启 | `66` | `150` | 50 | — |
| after the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 4

5` |
| after the bleed: 重启 | `66` | `150` | 50 | — |
| after the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 | — |

So the old geometry sat **+6 device px (≈2 CSS px)** right of the gear — the 2px the
CSS predicted —

and the shipped geometry lands within **1 device px** on the icon and
**exactly 0** on the label. T

he two row centres are 175 device px apart, which is

## Why the restart works this way

The obvious implementation is not available, and each dead end was verified
against the installed bu
ild rather than assumed:

- **The button cannot go inside the account menu.** Its items (`settings`,
`contact`, `signout`) are

a hard-coded array in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-account`; the menu exposes no plugin sea

t.
- **There is no restart API for plugins.** `window.dshDesktop` exposes only
`browser`, `deviceInf

o`, `keyboard`, `shortcuts` and `updates`; none of the 25
`dsh-desktop:*` IPC channels restarts anyt

hing. The Host is a plain Node child
of the Electron main process (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`), so it

cannot call
`app.relaunch()`. The built-in "Restart App and Host" menu item exists but is
gated on `

!app.isPackaged`, so a released build never shows it.
- **Closing the window does not quit.** `windo

w.on('close')` hides to the tray.
Launching the app again is also a no-op: the single-instance lock

turns the
second launch into "focus the existing window".

So the restart is an out-of-process handoff: the Host answers `202`, then a
detached helper kills th

e Electron main process and the Host **by PID**, waits
until both are really gone (which is what kee

ps the relaunch from being demoted
by the single-instance lock), and starts the application again wi

th the Node-mode
marker removed.
## What the tab does while that happens

The page cannot be told "restart finished" by a connection that is being torn
down, so after the `20

2` it polls the status route and compares the **boot id**.
A different boot id means the *new* proce

ss is answering, and the tab then calls
`location.reload()`. That reload is the point of the whole f

eature: it is what puts
the browser on the newly installed bundle instead of leaving it on the old c

ode —
and it is why the progress dialog is dismissable (Escape, the scrim, or its
button) rather tha

n a modal trap if the handoff never lands. The poll is read-only
and stops after `POLL_LIMIT` attemp
ts, handing the UI back.
## Endpoints
Both are same-origin, loopback-only.
| Route | Method | Purpose |
| `/dsh-desktop-restart/status` | GET | boot id, PIDs, and whether a restart is possible here (with

the reason when it is not) |
| `/dsh-desktop-restart/restart` | POST | performs the restart; answers
`202` before the app is killed |

`POST` refuses any request that carries a forwarding header, does not come from
loopback, has an `Or

igin` that disagrees with `Host`, or is not
`application/json` (a cross-site page cannot send that c

ontent type without a
